objective: Explain how an affine score becomes a binary probability and why preprocessing fits only training rows.
steps: Inspect source columns and the split. Row identities in training and validation must not overlap.
Fit the scaler on training rows and apply that same state to both partitions. Validation does not influence fitted preprocessing.
Fit logistic regression: X is an N×2 matrix, w is a length-2 coefficient vector, b is an optional scalar. Each row produces one decision score.
The sigmoid maps the score to a probability. Positive scores predict class 1; zero and negative scores predict class 0. A large score is confidence, not proof of correctness.
Inspect validation accuracy and log loss together. Confident wrong predictions can have a large loss even when accuracy looks acceptable.
Change C while keeping the prepared split fixed. Smaller C strengthens L2 regularization; there is no minibatch size or initialization seed for this deterministic full-batch lbfgs configuration.
Reload state.json and compare probabilities. Portable inference expects already-prepared feature values in the same order; it does not silently apply the scaler.
exercise: Compute z and sigmoid(z) for one held-out row using saved coefficients. Explain the class prediction and compare it with the recorded decision score.
assessment: Starter reading and runnable example only; no scored mastery receipt.
limits: Binary dense CPU classifier; no partial fitting, warm restart, GPU, shared autograd, or framework-wide coverage. A convergence warning remains visible in the run record.
title: A linear boundary
